children: What happened?
A number of stocks jumped in the afternoon session after an AI and chip sell-off pushed the S&P 500 into correction territory and drove traders into defensive shares.

Tech selling deepened as Anthropic fell more than 10% a day after its Nasdaq debut while Nvidia slid over 7% and AMD dropped 11%, leaving the Nasdaq down more than 3%, CNBC data showed. Fed Governor Lisa Cook warned in remarks covered by CNBC against delaying rate hikes.

Steady grocery demand from the previous session reinforced the bid after Walmart's earnings results showed Q3 revenue up 5.2% to $188.8 billion and a raised outlook, with CFO John David Rainey citing mid-single-digit U.S. grocery growth on the call.

When growth valuations compress alongside rate-hike fears, capital rotates to household and grocery names with steadier cash flows. Packaged food's lead over big-box retailers suggests investors are favoring cheaper defensives with room to rebound rather than paying up for crowded retail leaders.
The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks.
Among others, the following stocks were impacted:
Shelf-stable food company B&G Foods jumped 7.3%. Is now the time to buy B&G Foods?

Zooming in on B&G Foods

B&G Foods’s shares are very volatile and have had 20 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today’s move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was 9 days ago when the stock gained 25.8% on the news that the company reported third-quarter 2026 financial results featuring 5.0% base business net sales growth and raised its full-year guidance.

According to a company press release, B&G Foods reported that net sales reached $459.8 million, with adjusted EBITDA totaling $81.8 million. The company additionally reported adjusted diluted earnings per share of $0.21 for the three-month period. Beyond the quarterly figures, B&G Foods raised its full-year 2026 net sales expectations to a range of $1.760 billion to $1.800 billion. Furthermore, the company increased its annual adjusted EBITDA guidance to between $280.0 million and $290.0 million. During the earnings call, CEO Robert Mills pointed to early wins in optimizing product mix and expanding distribution, particularly in spices, seasoning, and bulk vegetable oil channels.

Looking ahead, B&G Foods’ updated guidance reflects confidence in its ability to sustain profitable growth by balancing branded retail expansion with targeted opportunities in private label and food service.

B&G Foods is down 14.6% since the beginning of the year, and at $3.59 per share, it is trading 38.9% below its 52-week high of $5.87 from March 2026. Investors who bought $1,000 worth of B&G Foods’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at only $115.31.
